newsitem.title: POLAND: Opposition seeks to halt Polish insurer PZU's sale.
newsitem.headline: Opposition seeks to halt Polish insurer PZU's sale.

text.p: Poland's largest opposition party, Solidarity Election Action (AWS), on Monday demanded the government drop its plan to partially sell off the country's biggest insurer, state-owned PZU SA.

The AWS said PZU's management and some cabinet members had devised a plan that would allow the company to be sold cheaply to some domestic investors -- an allegation the insurer rejected as political campaigning before the September 21 general election.

"The privatisation of PZU in its currently proposed form is pathological and should be abandoned at once," AWS spokesman Tomasz Tywonek told a news conference. The AWS is the main challenger of the ruling ex-communists according to the latest opinion polls.
The AWS said the government should promptly restructure the company and sell it to a strong Western strategic investor.
Otherwise, PZU will not be able to face competition when Poland fully opens its insurance market to foreign companies in 1999, according to an AWS insurance analyst, Tomasz Truskawa.

Truskawa alleged PZU's management had manipulated its accounts which allowed the firm to report a loss last year --a move designed to sell it cheaply to two Polish investors; banking group Pekao SA and computer firm Prokom.
"PZU's loss last year did not stem from the firm's real problems but from accounting and financial tricks..., meant to push down the market value of the company," Truskawa told the conference.
"The whole game was designed to allow a certain group of people to take over PZU," he added, naming Pekao and Prokom.
He said the company reported substantial profits in the first three quarters of last year but then announced a 170 million zlotys ($49 million) loss for whole year.
PZU spokesman Marek Maszek denied all the allegations, saying they were merely political rhetoric.
"The PZU card is being played for political ends," he said.
He said the company suffered the loss because it had to make statutory reserves and sought a quick sell-off to obtain at least 600 million zlotys needed to secure mandatory safety ratios.
"I do not hide that Pekao and Prokom are among companies interested in PZU..., but they are just two among many others," Maszek told Reuters.
He earlier said July's catastrophic flooding, which might force PZU to pay about 568 million zlotys in damages, could diminish its attractiveness.
The government, whose economic council (KERM) last month approved the sale of up to 49 percent of shares to raise at least the necessary 600 million zlotys, has delayed a final decision on the sale.
Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska told Reuters the cabinet would discuss on Tuesday some aspects of the PZU's privatisation .
